titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 2/2006 (ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ މާލީ ސެކިއުރިޓީޒްއާބެހޭ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިސްލާހު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Maldives Securities Act (Law no. 2/2006) to let foreigners invest in securities licensed in the Maldives. Foreign investment would be allowed only within the sectors set out in the Business Registration Act (Law no. 18/2014) and under rules made under the Securities Act. The Authority would write regulations on which securities foreigners may buy, what conditions foreign investors must meet, and how they trade on the stock exchange. It would also have to set up a system to monitor these trades. The changes would take effect three months after the law is ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whyItMatters: Foreign individuals and companies could buy and sell certain Maldivian securities on the stock exchange, under conditions set by the Authority. Which securities are open to them would be decided together with the ministry in charge of economic policy.
keyProvisions: Article 1 re-letters several paragraphs of Article 10 and adds a new paragraph. It covers deciding how foreigners may invest in securities licensed under the Act, within the sectors set by the Business Registration Act (18/2014).

Article 2 adds a new Article 41-1, 'Foreign investment in securities'. Under 41-1(a), foreigners may invest in securities within the Business Registration Act's sectors and in line with the Securities Act and its regulations.

Under 41-1(b), the regulations must cover three things: (1) which types of securities foreigners may invest in, (2) the conditions foreign investors must meet, and (3) the procedures for foreigners trading on the stock exchange.

Under 41-1(c), the Authority must set up a monitoring and compliance mechanism to check that foreign trades on the stock exchange follow the Business Registration Act, the Securities Act and its regulations. Under 41-1(d), the Authority decides which securities are open to foreigners after consulting the ministry responsible for economic policy.
Article 3 adds item (14) to Article 63(b): a regulation on foreign investors investing in securities.
Article 4 says the amendment takes effect three months after it is passed, ratified and published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Foreign investors, companies whose securities trade on the Maldives stock exchange, and the Authority that regulates securities.
statedReasons: The government says the bill sets the rules for foreigners to invest in Maldives-licensed securities markets, in line with the Business Registration Act (18/2014).
